nodes.label: HoneBill backend review
nodes.rationale: Point-in-time review of apps/backend on 2026-11-05. Re-verify findings before acting because the code changes.

nodes.label: ApiThrottlerGuard
nodes.rationale: Imported by wallet.controller.ts and never used. The global guard is plain ThrottlerGuard, and the exception filter reshapes the 429 body.

nodes.label: SettlementReconciliationService
nodes.rationale: Lives in reconciliation.util.ts. The *.util.ts name hides a service.

nodes.label: Settlement design
nodes.rationale: Unique nonce is the idempotency key. txHash and signedTxXdr are persisted before submit so a crash resumes instead of double-spending. The relayer lock uses a token-checked Lua release in a finally. BullMQ jobId is deterministic, retries are split from UnrecoverableError, and failed jobs are retained.

nodes.label: Webhook authentication
nodes.rationale: The SMS webhook uses raw bytes, a 2 KB cap, a timestamp drift window, and an HMAC, and it verifies the signature before JSON parsing.

nodes.label: Security hygiene
nodes.rationale: scrypt PIN hashing with transparent rehash, atomic Lua counters for PIN lockout and OTP attempts, JWT checks with explicit algorithms and issuer, ValidationPipe whitelist and forbidNonWhitelisted, PIN stripped from the register response, masked phone numbers in logs, and a git-ignored .env.

nodes.label: Boot-time env validation
nodes.rationale: Joi validates env vars at boot, and configureApp is shared so e2e tests run the same pipeline as production.

nodes.label: Optional infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Dynamic modules use register(enabled) with @Optional() fallbacks so BullMQ workers are not required for the process to boot.

nodes.label: Strong test culture
nodes.rationale: Many unit specs, e2e specs, and parity scripts against the legacy API. Nothing was executed for this review.

nodes.label: H1. Client-controlled IP used for abuse limits
nodes.rationale: otp.controller.ts builds the client IP from X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP before req.ip, and the anchor controller forwards those headers. There is no trust proxy setting, so a fresh X-Forwarded-For bypasses the per-IP OTP window and can exhaust the global cap. Verified.

nodes.label: H2. Production can boot with fake/insecure defaults
nodes.rationale: CORS_ORIGIN defaults to * and DATABASE_URL to a mock Postgres URL, including a PrismaService fallback when NODE_ENV is unset. Required secrets are optional(), so production can boot and fail on first use. Verified.

nodes.label: H3. phoneNumber is not unique but is treated as an identity
nodes.rationale: The schema only indexes phoneNumber. register is check-then-insert, so two concurrent registrations can both succeed, and verifyPin and checkUser use findFirst. Verified.

nodes.label: M1. No graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: enableShutdownHooks appears nowhere in src. PrismaService and RedisService onModuleDestroy do not run on SIGTERM, and BullMQ workers can be killed mid-job. Verified.

nodes.label: M2. Rate limiting is per-process, not shared
nodes.rationale: ThrottlerModule.forRoot uses the default in-memory store, so N instances multiply the limit and a restart resets it. WalletModule also calls forRoot a second time. Verified.

nodes.label: M3. Same provider registered in two modules
nodes.rationale: OtpRateLimitService is provided by both RedisModule and OtpModule, so Nest builds two instances. Two classes named StellarTransactionManager exist; SettlementsService uses the engine copy and StellarModule exports the infra copy. Verified.

nodes.label: M4. Offline signing intent has no freshness
nodes.rationale: Ed25519SignatureGuard signs deposit, withdraw, and transfer intent strings with no nonce or timestamp, so a captured Authorization can be replayed for the same sender and amount. Impact is bounded because the route returns unsigned XDR. Suspected.

nodes.label: M5. Signature verification falls back to a weaker format
nodes.rationale: If the contract-bound voucher signature fails, verification accepts a signature over the tuple without the contract address. That signature could be replayed against another deployment that shares token, gateway, and receiver. Suspected.

nodes.label: M6. A legitimate voucher can be silently dropped
nodes.rationale: SmsService.allowWebhookSender allows 3 webhooks per sender per minute and returns 200 {status: Rate Limited} when exceeded, so the gateway does not retry and the voucher is dropped. Verified.

nodes.label: M7. Validation duplicated and logic in controllers
nodes.rationale: RegisterAccountDto and AccountsService.register both validate the same fields, and AccountsController and AuthController parse bodies. The duplication exists for legacy error-body parity and leaves two sources of truth. Verified.

nodes.label: M8. Env vars used but not in the schema
nodes.rationale: SEP10_HOME_DOMAINS is required at runtime but absent from the Joi schema. health.controller and engine.module read process.env directly. DEMO_ENABLED and OTP_GLOBAL_LIMIT_PER_HOUR are also read without schema entries. Verified.

nodes.label: M9. Docs and Swagger are mostly empty
nodes.rationale: No @ApiProperty or @ApiTags, and nest-cli.json has no @nestjs/swagger plugin, so /api/docs lists routes with empty schemas. Swagger is public in production. Verified.

nodes.label: L1. Docker/port mismatch
nodes.rationale: The Dockerfile exposes and health-checks port 3001 while main.ts listens on PORT or 3000. The health check calls /api/docs-json instead of the health route, and the runtime image copies dev dependencies. Verified.

nodes.label: L2. Broken/duplicate npm script
nodes.rationale: package.json defines test:e2e:phase2 twice. JSON keeps the last definition, which points at a Jest config and paths that no longer exist. Verified.

nodes.label: L3. Repo hygiene
nodes.rationale: Tracked logs, parity output, and *.tmp.mjs scripts under apps/backend are noise and a leak risk. e2e specs and unit specs are also duplicated in a second folder. Verified.

nodes.label: L4. Naming
nodes.rationale: WalletService, SettlementsService, and SettlementReconciliationService live in *.util.ts files. Settlement.qstashMessageId stores an unrelated engine-<nonce> value. Verified.

nodes.label: L5. Missing hardening middleware
nodes.rationale: helmet and compression are not dependencies. CORS_ORIGIN defaults to *, which is the same default called out in H2. Verified.

nodes.label: L6. Account enumeration surfaces
nodes.rationale: verifyPin returns 404 Account not found versus 401 for a wrong PIN, and /users/check returns exists plus keys for any phone. Verified.

nodes.label: L7. PIN strength is bounded by its length
nodes.rationale: PINs are 4-6 digits. scrypt slows guessing and online lockout is strong, but a leaked database is still crackable offline. Legacy plaintext PINs are upgraded on successful verify. Verified design note.

nodes.label: L8. Hard-coded business constant
nodes.rationale: The 5_000_000n protocol toll for PHPC is embedded in settlements.util.ts, so a fee change requires a redeploy. Verified.

nodes.label: L9. Relayer lock scope
nodes.rationale: The lock is released after sendTransaction and before inclusion, so a second job can reuse the sequence number and hit tx_bad_seq. The retry policy treats that as retryable, so it self-heals at the cost of wasted attempts. Suspected.

nodes.label: L10. Unused imports and dead guard
nodes.rationale: wallet.controller.ts imports UseGuards and ApiThrottlerGuard without using them. ApiThrottlerGuard itself is unused. Verified.
